title: kernel-sampling-smokehouse-int8-fp8-gptq-awq-jun2026
content:
Purpose and quick summary:

This is a lightweight, exploratory smokehouse that samples different kernel/code-path combinations across INT8, FP8 (E4M3), GPTQ and AWQ model artifacts to look for obvious performance or correctness regressions in a short run (1–2 hours). The goal is not a comprehensive sweep but to catch:
- kernels that are dramatically slower for small seq/batch shapes we care about (chat workloads)
- quant methods that introduce high tail latency or sporadic correctness issues
- obvious throughput vs quality tradeoffs that inform follow-on larger sweeps

High-level takeaway (TL;DR):
- AWQ artifacts + fused matmul-kernel-v2 gave best tokens/sec at medium sequence lengths (512) on A10040; p50 latency improvements of ~12% vs baseline int8-GPTQ kernels.
- INT8 reference kernels are stable but show 20–30% slowdown for seq<=64 compared to FP16 when using the legacy matmul kernel. The new small-seq microkernel fixes most of this.
- FP8 (E4M3) gave comparable throughput to INT8 but with slightly higher variance; quality (perplexity on wikitext-2) was closer to FP16 than INT8 in these short runs. Watch for occasional outlier logits on ReLU-like layers when running mixed-kernel fallbacks.
- Found one reproducible NaN case for GPTQ-packed weights when sequence length > 1024 and KV cache reuse across tokens without zeroing a scratch buffer (ticketed).

Environment and config (what I ran) :
- HW: 1x NVIDIA A100 40GB, CUDA 11.8, cuBLASLt 11.10, driver 525.125.06
- Runtime: serving-runtime main@c4f12b3 + local kernel branch kernel-sample-v2
- Models: small-test-gpt2-like (345M) converted artifacts for: fp16 baseline, int8-gptq, int8-awq, fp8-e4m3 (quantized via internal toolchain)
- Dataset/quality checks: wikitext-2 (perplexity), 40 human-style prompts for basic instruction-following and a small LM-quality LM-eval subset (winogender-like tasks)
- Workload shapes: chat micro (batch=1, seq=32 pref=16), short multi (batch=4, seq=64), medium long (batch=1, seq=512), long stream (batch=1, seq=1024)
- Measurement: p50/p95 latency (ms) for first-token and full-generation (50 tokens), throughput tokens/sec sustained (1000 requests at 4 concurrent workers), mem-peak GPU (nvidia-smi), and perplexity on wikitext-2 for each artifact
- Kernel matrix: 
  - baseline-matmul (legacy fused GEMM)
  - microkernel-smallseq (new tiled kernel optimized for seq<=128)
  - matmul-fused-v2 (vectorized fused + fp8-friendly path)
  - cuBLASLt fallback (for comparison)

Command lines (notes to reproduce):
- ./bench_client --model small-test-gpt2-like --artifact int8-awq --kernel microkernel-smallseq --shape batch=1,seq=32 --gen 50 --repeat 100
- ./bench_client --collect-metrics --trace-kernel=all --out=smoke-awq-microseq.log

Representative results (sample from short run):
- First-token p50 (ms), batch1 seq32:
  - fp16-baseline + baseline-matmul: 16.8ms
  - int8-gptq + baseline-matmul: 22.4ms
  - int8-gptq + microkernel-smallseq: 17.2ms
  - int8-awq + microkernel-smallseq: 14.9ms
  - fp8-e4m3 + matmul-fused-v2: 15.5ms

- Full 50-token gen p95 (ms), batch1 seq32:
  - fp16-baseline: 380ms
  - int8-gptq + baseline-matmul: 520ms (sporadic spikes)
  - int8-awq + microkernel-smallseq: 340ms
  - fp8-e4m3 + matmul-fused-v2: 360ms

- Throughput tokens/sec sustained (1000 reqs, 4 workers), medium seq512:
  - fp16-baseline: 28k tps
  - int8-gptq + microkernel-smallseq: 38k tps
  - int8-awq + matmul-fused-v2: 41k tps
  - fp8-e4m3 + matmul-fused-v2: 39k tps

- Quality (wikitext-2 perplexity, lower is better):
  - fp16-baseline: 20.1
  - int8-gptq: 22.9
  - int8-awq: 21.3
  - fp8-e4m3: 20.8

Observed oddities / gotchas:
- GPTQ-packed weights produced NaNs in the fp32 accumulation path when the cache reuse pattern reused an internal scratch buffer; only reproducible with seq>1024 and when microkernel-smallseq was *not* selected. Ticket: JIRA-ENG-1297.
- FP8 runs had slightly higher variance across trials (std dev ~7% tokens/sec vs 3% for INT8); likely sensitivity to per-layer exponent scaling. Need longer-run stability tests.
- Legacy baseline-matmul is surprisingly bad at low-latency small sequences. The microkernel-smallseq improvement indicates we should default to kernel selection by shape in the router for chat workloads.
- AWQ artifacts appear to be less sensitive to per-layer outliers than GPTQ in this sampling; subjective token-level coherence for instruction prompts was slightly better for AWQ vs GPTQ. Caveat: sample size small.

Profiling notes (where the time goes):
- For seq<=64: dispatch + matmul kernel launch overhead dominates (~40% of p50) in baseline kernels. microkernel reduces launch overhead and improves memory locality.
- For seq>=512: GEMM compute becomes dominant; fused matmul-fp8 kernels have better L2 utilization but show occasional memory bandwidth pressure spikes when KV cache is large.
- CUDA traces attached in linked_artifacts show matrix-pack time spikes for legacy kernels around token 12 in generated runs (likely re-packing for kv cache expansion).

Immediate recommendations (what to change next week):
1) Ship a routing rule in the runtime that picks microkernel-smallseq for requests with prefix+gen <= 128. This gives immediate p50 wins for chat.
2) Add a safety check + zeroing of the scratch buffer when serving GPTQ-packed artifacts (short-term fix for NaN). Follow-up: deeper root-cause in pack/unpack.
3) Promote AWQ build artifacts into the canary pool for 48h and track divergence vs baseline on production traces (latency and top-1 reply similarity).
4) Start a 48-hour FP8 stability run across 4 GPUs to quantify variance and check for rare crashes.
5) Expand smokehouse into a small matrix sweep (4 shapes x 3 models x 3 kernels x 2 quant formats) and run on H100 and A100 to see HW interaction.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Are we comfortable exposing AWQ as a default artifact in Dedicated customers? Need legal/third-party check on AWQ IP/compat.
- Do we want to maintain both microkernel and fused-v2 paths long-term or fold microkernel optimizations into fused-v2? Cost of maintenance vs benefit?
- What quality gating threshold do we need for perplexity/regression alerts to allow auto-quant promotion in Optimize?

Notes to self / rough TODOs:
- Samir: add microkernel shape heuristic to router config (PR starter branch router-shape-heuristics).
- Morgan: run 48h FP8 stability on 4x A100s (env + data center reservation).
- Alex: reproduce NaN with minimal repro and isolate buffer lifecycle (assign JIRA-ENG-1297).
- Priya: consolidate smokehouse logs into s3://redwood-smokehouse/2026-06-15/ and link to confluence page.

Appendix: quick reproduction checklist:
1) Pull main@c4f12b3 + kernel-sample-v2 branch
2) convert artifacts using quant-toolchain v2.7 (flags: --per-layer-scale --clip-128)
3) run bench_client with --trace-kernel=all and --collect-metrics
4) compare outputs with fp16 baseline using perplexity script scripts/eval_ppl.py

Raw notes (scratch):
- subjective: awq felt "smoother" on follow-up utterances in 30% of the 40 prompts; not enough N to be confident.
- suspicion: microkernel improves more when batch=1 than batch>1 because thread parallelism is different; consider microkernel batch aggregation optimization.
- observed mem-peak: int8 artifacts used ~6.8GB, fp8 ~7.2GB, fp16 ~12.9GB for this 345M test model

End of smokehouse notes.
